title: Static friction can stop a slide from starting
summary: Static friction is the force that prevents slipping while two surfaces are not yet sliding.
body: OpenStax Physics separates kinds of friction. Kinetic friction opposes a slide that is already happening and slows it. Static friction is the case where friction prevents the object from sliding at all. The page also says the size of friction depends on a coefficient, set by the nature of the two surfaces, and on the normal force pressing them together. Urone and Hinrichs, 26 March 2020. A heavy crate that will not budge until the push is large enough is the static case.
